newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mixed, palladium surges.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mixed, palladium surges.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mixed on Wednesday, with palladium futures jumping on heavy buying from Engelhard Corp, while gold futures slipped on the yen's firmness and weaker bullion prices, Japanese traders said.
July palladium, which has no limit, surged by 35 yen per gram at 716 yen. All other futures rose by 22 yen per gram, with benchmark June ending up 22 yen at 525 yen.
Further delays in the resumption of Russian platinum group metals (PGM) shipments to Japan were also cited as a bullish factor, the traders said.

"Sentiment towards PGMs is bullish," an analyst at a commodity broker said. "A large overhang of TOCOM short positions, especially in palladium, combined with the extremely tight physical market, were cited as bullish factors," he said.

Another trader echoed the views, saying the PGM market has been very sensitive to bullish factors. Platinum futures ranged from two yen to 12 yen per gram higher. Benchmark June was up four yen at 1,357 yen.
After lacklustre trade, TOCOM gold futures ended lower as early bargain-hunting buying ebbed reflecting a further slip in spot gold prices.
In the spot market, bullion was quoted at $331.70/332.00 per ounce at 0820 GMT, against New York's $333.70/20.

"In the bullion market, hedge selling by Australian producers continued to dent spot gold prices," a trading house trader said. "Spot gold may probe the downside at $330 per ounce in the near future," the trader said.
Concern over possible European central bank sales and a lack of inflationary fears were behind the weak gold market.
Gold futures ranged from nine yen to 14 yen per gram lower. Benchmark June gold was off 13 yen at 1,213 yen. Benchmark June silver was off 0.5 yen per 10 grams at 173.6 yen.
